cohort: The study included 423 neonates admitted to Neonatal Intensive Care Units (NICUs) of three tertiary hospitals in Mogadishu, Somalia, along with their mothers.
finding: The overall prevalence of neonatal jaundice was 30.26%, with higher maternal age, prolonged labour, ABO and Rh incompatibility, and neonatal sepsis identified as significant risk factors.
mod_finding: Neonates delivered vaginally had a significantly higher risk of neonatal jaundice compared with those delivered by caesarean section.
cross-section timing: During admission to Neonatal Intensive Care Units
